cards.title: Partner's Behavior at Kids' Football Matches
cards.body: A long-term partner's aggressive conduct at sons' football matches is straining the relationship. An advice columnist suggests having a calm conversation to understand the root of his anger rather than focusing solely on his inappropriate behavior.

cards.title: Halloween Magic and Family Connection
cards.body: A parent ditches cynicism to embrace Halloween celebrations as a moment of magic with their kids. From Day of the Dead traditions to Samhain, autumn festivities offer centuries-old ways to connect as a family.

cards.title: Why Kids Say 'Na-Na-Na' So Annoyingly
cards.body: A reader explores the psychology behind why children's repetitive chants like 'na-na-na' are so annoying to adults. The Guardian's long-running series answers curious questions about child behavior.

cards.title: Helping Traumatized Children With Severe Behaviors
cards.body: Strong fears often drive troubling behaviors in children, particularly those in adoptive, foster, or reconstituted families. Practical strategies can help parents and caregivers address underlying trauma rather than just managing surface-level conduct.

cards.title: Boredom Is Uncomfortable—And That's Okay
cards.body: When kids complain they're bored, parents' instinct is often to fix it immediately. However, allowing children to sit with boredom may actually be developmentally beneficial rather than harmful.

cards.title: Childhood Cancer Symptoms Can Be Easily Missed
cards.body: Although rare, cancer is the leading cause of death from disease among children under 15 in the UK. Parents should be aware of warning signs that are often overlooked in early stages.

cards.title: Teen Mental Health Beyond Screens
cards.body: A Psychology Today article examines what parents and experts might be getting wrong about kids' technology use and mental health. The piece challenges common assumptions about screen time and adolescent wellbeing.
